questions.q: A nibble consists of how many bits?
questions.solution: A nibble is half a byte: 4 bits. A byte is 8 bits; a word is CPU-dependent (16/32/64 bits).
questions.shortcut: Nibble = half a byte = 4 bits ('nybble nibbles off half').

questions.q: Under the IT Act, cyber terrorism is dealt with in:
questions.solution: Section 66F covers cyber terrorism - acts threatening India's sovereignty, integrity or security through computers - punishable with imprisonment that may extend to life.
questions.shortcut: 66F = Fearsome (terrorism); 66C identity, 66D personation-cheating.

questions.q: Which shortcut takes a web browser back to the previously visited page?
questions.solution: Alt+Left goes back and Alt+Right goes forward. Alt+Home opens the home page, and Ctrl+Left moves the cursor one word left in a text box.
questions.shortcut: Alt+arrows = time travel through history.

questions.q: In MS Excel, pressing Ctrl+Space selects:
questions.solution: Ctrl+Space selects the whole column of the active cell and Shift+Space selects the whole row. Ctrl+A selects the data region, or the whole sheet if pressed again.
questions.shortcut: Ctrl and Column both start with C; Shift+Space = row.

questions.q:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

A white elephant
questions.solution: Kings once gifted white elephants whose upkeep ruined the receiver — grand to own, ruinous to keep → **a costly, useless possession**. The sacred/rare options take the colour literally.
questions.shortcut: Upkeep test: does keeping it drain you? That is the white elephant.

questions.q:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The paediatrician ___ the mother to complete the full course of medicine.
questions.solution: The sentence needs a finite past verb after its subject: **advised**. *Advice* is a noun, *advices* is not standard English, *advising* cannot serve alone as the verb.
questions.shortcut: Frame first: subject + blank + object → finite verb → advised.

questions.q: Select the correctly spelt word.
questions.solution: Keep the **e** before -able: noticeable. The e protects the soft 'c' sound (notice → notice-able). Noticable is the planted drop.
questions.shortcut: Keep-e rule: soft c needs its e.

questions.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number (5).
questions.solution: Strip the sentence to its skeleton: 'a group ___ its own quiet discipline'. The subject *a group* is singular and the passage speaks in general present, so: **develops**. *Develop* lacks agreement; *developing* cannot serve as the finite verb; *had developed* drags in a past perfect that has no anchor in this habitual, timeless statement.
questions.shortcut: Skeleton test: 'a group ___' → singular present, -s form.

questions.q: The slogan **'Do or Die'** was given by Gandhi during the —
questions.solution: Gandhi gave the call 'Do or Die' on **8 August 1942** at **Gowalia Tank, Bombay**, when the Quit India resolution was passed.
questions.shortcut: 1942 = last big push → last-chance slogan 'Do or Die'.

questions.q: The five-kingdom classification of living organisms was proposed by:
questions.solution: **R.H. Whittaker** proposed the five kingdoms — Monera, Protista, Fungi, Plantae, Animalia — in **1969**. Linnaeus gave binomial nomenclature and the two-kingdom system.
questions.shortcut: My Pet Fish Plays Alone — Whittaker.

questions.q: Which Delhi Sultan introduced the silver **tanka** and the copper **jital**?
questions.solution: **Iltutmish** issued the standard Arabic coins — silver tanka and copper jital — and also organised the **iqta** system and the Group of Forty.
questions.shortcut: **I**ltutmish = **I**qta + **I**deal coins.

questions.q: Hydraulic brakes in vehicles work on the principle of:
questions.solution: **Pascal's law**: pressure applied to an enclosed incompressible fluid is transmitted equally in all directions. Hydraulic brakes, lifts and presses use it.
questions.shortcut: Anything 'hydraulic' → Pascal.

questions.q: A sum amounts to ₹4,840 in 2 years at 10% per annum compound interest. The sum is:
The simple interest on a certain sum for 2 years is ₹800 and the compound interest for the same period is ₹832. The rate of interest per annum is:
questions.shortcut: Ratio trick: gap/SI = R/200 ⇒ 32/800 = R/200 ⇒ R = 8%.

questions.q: The price of an article falls from ₹250 to ₹200. The percentage decrease in price is:
questions.solution:
Decrease $= 50$ on the original ₹250.
$\frac{50}{250} \times 100 = 20\%$.
questions.shortcut: Base is the ORIGINAL 250, not 200. 50/250 = 1/5 = 20%.

questions.q: The incomes of A and B are in the ratio 8 : 5 and their expenditures are in the ratio 5 : 3. If each saves ₹1,200, then A's income is:
questions.solution:
Incomes 8x, 5x; expenditures 5y, 3y.
8x − 5y = 1200 and 5x − 3y = 1200.
Subtracting: 3x − 2y = 0 ⇒ y = 1.5x. Then 5x − 4.5x = 1200 ⇒ x = 2400.
A's income = $8 \times 2400$ = ₹19,200.
questions.shortcut: Two equations, subtract to kill one variable: y = 1.5x ⇒ 0.5x = 1200 ⇒ A = 8x = ₹19,200.

questions.solution: The correct figure sits in the **lower-right part** of the given figure, with every line matching in direction and length. The other three options are the same shape shown as its mirror (left-right flip), a water image (top-bottom flip) and a copy turned through 90 degrees — none of them can be traced in the figure without turning it, and rotation is not allowed.
questions.shortcut: Fix the most distinctive stroke (a lone diagonal or an odd-length line), locate it in the main figure, then check the rest.

questions.q:
**Statements:** All rings are circles. Some circles are squares. No square is a triangle.

**Conclusions:** I. Some circles are triangles. II. No circle is a triangle.
options: Either conclusion I or II follows
questions.solution: Neither I nor II is forced (circles may or may not touch triangles). They are negation pairs about circles-triangles, so they can't both fail. **Either-or.**
questions.shortcut: Even with three statements, the pair test only needs the two conclusion terms.

questions.q: In a queue of **50 people, X is 16th from the front and Y is 20th from the back.** How many people are **between** X and Y?
questions.solution: Y from the front = 50 + 1 − 20 = 31st. Between = 31 − 16 − 1 = **14**.
questions.shortcut: Same-end conversion first; then difference − 1.

questions.q: In a certain code, **PLANET** is written as **LPNATE**. How is **GARDEN** written in that code?
questions.solution: PLANET → PL | AN | ET → LP | NA | TE: each pair of letters is swapped. GARDEN → GA | RD | EN → **AGDRNE**.
questions.shortcut: Same letters in the code = rearrangement. Swap in pairs from the left.
